head: split/independent-library
title: Build independent AutoLimit library with standalone and AutoAuth integration tests
body:
AutoLimit becomes an independent Java 21 Gradle library with Spring Boot servlet auto-configuration. It works without AutoAuth, JWT keys, JJWT, Swagger, Redis, or Spring Security.

Implementation:
- Copy RateLimit/UserQuota, RateLimitAspect, RateLimitService, IpRateLimitFilter, CallerIdentity/CallerIdentityResolver, the exception, and the renamed AutoLimitRateLimitExceptionResolver from verified AutoAuth separate-auth-limit at d388ffd135fec8ab6307bdef9d9bcee067ee43fc.
- Move all packages/imports, tests, Javadoc references, and AOP pointcut annotation names to com.autolimit.
- Carry over the existing local resolver-focused test preparation.
- Add autolimit properties and Boot auto-configuration imports/configuration metadata.
- Provide overridable limiter, aspect, anonymous resolver, 429 resolver, IP filter, and named filter registration beans.
- Register the IP filter once in the servlet container at order -110, before Boot's default security order -100, for REQUEST dispatches only.
- Resolve authenticated user IDs and roles through the application SPI; empty means anonymous, and provider failures propagate.

The base build has no AutoAuth dependency. Code importing both libraries is isolated in examples/autoauth-integration, an independent consuming composite build. It supplies the AuthContext identity bridge and tests actual JWT identities and roles. The original AutoLimit repository/history and existing files are retained; the README includes source attribution.

Validation run locally with Java 21 / Gradle 9:
- .\gradlew.bat build: PASS, 25 standalone tests, zero failures/errors/skips; also passed from the original repository checkout.
- .\gradlew.bat dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath and testRuntimeClasspath: inspected; no AutoAuth, Spring Security, JJWT, or Swagger.
- .\gradlew.bat -p examples/autoauth-integration -PautoauthDir=<AutoAuth checkout> build: PASS, 3 real-HTTP integration tests. They verify per-user and highest-role quotas, anonymous quotas/429, authentication, exactly one IP filter invocation per request, no IP filter inside the security chain, and early IP rejection skipping JWT validation and endpoint quotas.
- Integration runtime dependency tree inspected after its Swagger exclusion; both source libraries resolve on the existing Boot 3.2.4 baseline.
- AutoAuth companion build: PASS, 89 tests; its runtime/test dependency trees contain no AutoLimit.
- JAR metadata/classes and whitespace checks inspected.

Standalone coverage includes Boot discovery with forbidden authentication classes absent, anonymous limits, user/role quotas, default and overridden beans, resolver failures, filter configuration/disablement, and JSON 429 handling.

Companion: [AutoAuth extraction branch]().

Consumer migration:
Add com.autolimit:autolimit:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT from a local/source build (no release is published here), update limiter imports and resolver class name, move autoauth.pre-auth-rate-limit to autolimit.pre-auth-rate-limit, and provide CallerIdentityResolver for authenticated quotas. Do not also install the IP filter in a security chain. See README.md and examples/autoauth-integration/README.md.

Existing concerns outside the split:
- The retained limiter uses per-process, non-atomic endpoint counters, method-name keys that can collide across controllers, and 15-minute idle eviction even for longer windows. IP resolution trusts the first forwarded header value.
- AutoAuth's existing springdoc 2.8.17 dependency mixes Boot 3.5 components with the 3.2.4 baseline and broke initial full application startup. The consuming example excludes that optional UI starter; neither library's dependency versions were upgraded.
- Javadoc and existing AutoAuth unchecked-operation warnings remain; all builds above completed successfully.
